name: Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN)
note: Maldives's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: MIRA issues TINs only to those required to register with it (individuals for income tax when their monthly average income from business or from several employments exceeds MVR 40,000 in a 12-month period, among others); each taxpayer gets a unique seven-digit business-partner number and each tax registration a TIN made of it, the revenue code and a sequence number; an individual's income-tax TIN reads like 1000001PIT001. The format holds the individual income-tax TIN (seven digits, PIT, three digits). Read as given on registration, to anyone required to register; needed for tax. The Maldives' national identity card number (the Department of National Registration's) isn't read here. No check rule, age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Maldives: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Individuals = 1000001PIT001 ... TIN is only issued if the taxpayer is required to register at MIRA under any of the tax admin requirements. ... So for each taxpayer MIRA issues a unique 7 digit identifier. ... {BP}{Revenue Code}{incrementing Number}
